title: Protocol for measurement of calcium dysregulation in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived dopaminergic neurons
protocol: Prepare HEPES-buffered ACSF.
Dissolve 1 mM stock solution of Fluo-4-AM with neurobasal medium to a final concentration of 2 μM.
Load 1 mL of Fluo-4-AM working solution (2 μM) to human DA neurons plated on cover glasses.
Incubate neurons in a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator for 30 min.
Remove Fluo-4-AM working solution from neurons.
Wash neurons three times with HEPES-buffered ACSF.
Incubate neurons at 22°C–25°C in the dark for additional 20–25 min to allow for complete dye de-esterification.
Place neurons in a 30°C–32°C heated adaptor.
Perform live-cell imaging by inverted confocal microscope LSM880 with a 40×/1.35NA oil-immersion objective.
Perfuse imaging chamber with warm HEPES-buffered ACSF solution at 30°C–32°C.
Keep ACSF perfusion rate at 1 mL/min.
Conduct live-cell imaging with excitation wavelength of 485 nm and emission wavelength of 525 nm.
Acquire images every second during the experiment.
Use a frequency of acquisition of 1.0 Hz.
Record basal activity for at least 5 minutes before applying stimuli.
Finish live-cell imaging within 2 hours after transferring neurons to the microscope.
Prepare external solution on the day of experiment.
Thaw intracellular solution on ice and keep it on ice throughout recording.
Select regions of interest (ROI) by drawing the outline of cell soma in Zen software.
Measure fluorescence intensity values for each time point.
Transfer data to statistical program (e.g., GraphPad Prism) for further analysis.
Prepare patch-clamp pipettes to achieve resistance of 3–5 MΩ.
Turn on all recording equipment.
Set up pump to perfuse external solution through the recording chamber at 1–2 mL/min.
Ensure continuous bubbling of external solution with 95% O₂ and 5% CO₂.
Maintain external solution temperature at 32°C using a temperature controller and in-line heater.
Transfer coverslip containing human DA neurons to the recording chamber, cells facing up.
Fill a 1 mL syringe with 200 μL of intracellular solution.
Attach a 0.2 μm pore filter and micro-loader tip to the syringe.
Use the syringe linked to the filter and micro-loader tip to fill the patch-clamp pipette with intracellular solution.
Tap the pipette gently to eliminate air bubbles in the tip.
Place the pipette in the pipette holder.
Insert the pipette tip into the bath and apply very light positive pressure using a three-way valve.
Search for and focus on a healthy neuron with a 40× water immersion objective.
Set the amplifier to voltage-clamp mode.
Correct the pipette offset so currents measured are considered as 0 pA.
Approach the selected soma with the patch-clamp pipette.
Release positive pressure and apply gentle suction to achieve gigaseal formation.
Change the voltage clamp to a negative voltage close to −60 mV or −70 mV.
Rupture the membrane by applying light and short suction pulses using a syringe.
Hold the cell at −60 mV in voltage-clamp configuration.
Record Ca2+ currents by stepping to various potentials from −60 mV to +50 mV for 250 ms in 10 mV increments.
Acquire data with PatchMaster software, sampled at 10 kHz and filtered at 2.9 kHz.
Slowly and carefully detach the pipette from the neuron to let the membrane reseal.
